items.summary: The security-research model scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, which turns known vulnerabilities into working exploits, against 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, and OpenAI reports it avoids out-of-scope services 99.93% of the time without deployment safety prompts (94.49% for its predecessor). It is Critical under the Preparedness Framework and available only via the API and Codex to selected Daybreak Red customers; OpenAI credits it with the 948 Linux privilege-escalation exploits of [[2026-11-06#0|yesterday's pipeline]] and 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox flaws.
items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Cyber, its first model rated Critical for cybersecurity

items.summary: Instead of emitting coordinates one token at a time, VFlash predicts points, boxes and trajectories jointly with a lightweight drafter in a single forward pass, measuring about 25x faster generation on 3D point motion forecasting in a single-rollout test. A world action model conditioned on its plans reaches 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites against 62.6% for the baseline — the opposite bet to [[2026-11-06#9|NEO-VLA's case for dropping the vision encoder]], keeping the perception stack and attacking the decoding cost instead.
items.title: NVIDIA's VFlash decodes visual primitives in one pass, ~25x faster than token-by-token

items.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.2% intraday on 5 November and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped about 9.75%, on track for its steepest daily loss since March 2020; AMD and Micron each lost roughly 15%, Qualcomm 11.2%, Arm 11% and Nvidia almost 9%. The trigger is the moratorium risk behind [[2026-11-06#8|the 41 data-centre ballot measures voters passed]] — Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants an immediate moratorium, and Wells Fargo puts 27% of planned US data-centre gigawatts in Texas.
items.title: Chip and AI stocks lose about $3T as data-centre ballot results sink in

items.summary: DOJ-SITF, led by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss, will prosecute misuse of SI by foreign and state-sponsored actors, transnational criminal organisations and corporate actors, with Attorney General Todd Blanche naming attacks on taxpayers, critical infrastructure and national security. It is the first dedicated US federal enforcement body for AI misuse and adopts the 'super intelligence' vocabulary of [[2026-09-28#0|the US–China dialogue agreed at the Trump–Xi summit]].
items.title: US Justice Department launches a Super Intelligence Task Force

items.summary: ByteDance Seed researchers train a sparse autoencoder on an MoE layer's output and decompose each latent's pre-activation exactly across experts, on layers 4, 30 and 46 of Qwen3-30B-A3B. Contribution is more concentrated than the gating weights suggest, most latents have one or two dominant experts, and auto-interpretation finds distinctions as fine as separate experts for Java and front-end web code, or geometry versus arithmetic; the SAEs and code are released.
items.title: Sparse autoencoders show MoE experts specialise in human-readable ways

items.summary: Conductor's product orchestrates multiple AI coding agents in parallel on one codebase; Meta is folding the team into its software-engineering work and terms were not disclosed. It is the second multi-agent coding tool to change hands or open up in a week, after [[2026-11-02#10|DeepSeek open-sourcing Super-Agent]].
items.title: Meta acquires Conductor, whose app runs several coding agents at once

lead: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, the first model it has classified as Critical for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, and is restricting it to selected Daybreak Red customers.
window: 6 Nov 07:00 → 7 Nov 07:00 JST (+ late catch from 4 Nov)
